newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawmakers reject motion on China over rights.
newsitem.headline: HK lawmakers reject motion on China over rights.

text.p: Hong Kong legislators on Wednesday rejected a motion urging the Chinese government to accede to two U.N. human-rights pacts, local radio reported.
In a legislature meeting, lawmakers voted 26 to 24 to reject the motion put forward by Democratic Party member John Tse.

He argued that Beijing should guarantee people in Hong Kong and China the rights covered by the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights.
But opponents said the chamber had no right to infringe on China's affairs, the radio said.
China has said it was considering signing the human-rights covenants, which would allow the international community to monitor its performance.
The British colony is set to revert to China on July 1 after a century and a half as a British colony.
Beijing's plans to slash civil liberties and democracy have raised fears over human rights in post-handover Hong Kong.
